title: Method overloading and overriding: the difference that trips people up

videos.script: Two words that sound alike and mean opposite things. This lesson is about telling them apart, because mixing them up compiles. {{overload}} Overloading is several methods with one name and different parameters. The compiler picks one from the arguments you wrote, before the program runs. Six calls to one name, and six different methods. {{rank}} When more than one would fit, the compiler has an order of preference. Widening first, boxing second, varargs last. And when two fit equally well, it refuses. {{override}} Overriding is a subclass replacing a method it inherited, with exactly the same signature. That choice is made while the program runs, by the object. {{typo}} One letter wrong in the name, and an override silently becomes a new method. The annotation at sign Override is what catches it. {{trap}} Last, the trap the lesson is named for: an equals method that takes a Book. It works when you call it, and a HashSet keeps two copies of the same book anyway.
